Bank and Cash Accounts — Edit

This form configures the control account for bank and cash accounts.

The control account determines where bank and cash balances appear on the balance sheet.

Name

Enter a descriptive name for this control account that groups similar bank accounts together.

Control accounts consolidate multiple bank accounts into a single line on financial reports.

Examples: 'Operating Bank Accounts', 'Investment Accounts', 'Restricted Funds', or 'Foreign Currency Accounts'.

Code

Enter an optional account code to identify this control account in reports and listings.

Account codes facilitate integration with other systems and make account selection faster.

Consider using a systematic numbering scheme like '1100' for operating accounts, '1200' for savings accounts.

Group

Select the balance sheet group that determines where this control account appears on financial statements.

Most bank accounts belong under 'Current Assets', but you may have specific groups for different account types.

The group selection affects how accounts are subtotaled and presented on the balance sheet.

Position

Enter a position number to control the display order of this account within its balance sheet group.

Lower numbers appear first. Use gaps (like 10, 20, 30) to allow inserting accounts later.

This helps organize your balance sheet in a logical order, such as listing operating accounts before investment accounts.

Inactive

Check this box to deactivate the control account without deleting it.

Inactive control accounts are hidden from selection lists but retain all historical data.

Use this when reorganizing your chart of accounts or phasing out old account groupings.
